thread:
sylvie: FYI we had a cascade of tiny-pod evictions in ap-southeast1 this morning. started when a subset of racks hit egress throttling on the ToR and kubelets began evicting sandboxed pods. packing went sideways.

haresh: saw the alerts. any kube events?

sylvie: kube events excerpt: 
```
Warning  Eviction    3m   kubelet    pod sandbox evicted: nic egress throttled, quota exceeded
Normal   Pulling     2m   kubelet    pulling image for preemptible-fractional
Normal   Preempted   1m   scheduler  Preempted pod=trainer-small uid=... (gpu=0.25)
```

omar: fractional GPU workloads are being scattered across many nodes; when a node's egress gets throttled we rebind and create more fragmentation. current scheduler doesn't consider node.egress_5m or rack_e2e_util.

nina: can we taint nodes that exceed an egress threshold so new pods avoid them? taint + toleration for low-prio would force only tolerant pods to land there.

haresh: tainting helps but immediate taints cause mass reschedules. we should avoid creating churn. propose: 1) a soft-taint (label) + scoring penalty initially, 2) escalate to taint if sustained high for N windows. hysteresis avoids flip-flop.

omar: agreed. scoring plugin sketch:
```
priorityPlugins:
  - name: gpu_fit
    weight: 100
  - name: egress_util_penalty
    weight: 60
    params:
      window_seconds: 300
      threshold_bytes: 1200000000  # 1.2GB/5m
      sustained_windows: 2
      linear_scale: 0.00000004
      taint_escalation_seconds: 600
```
The plugin returns a penalty score; if sustained it triggers node label/kubelet taint via controller.

sylvie: to isolate churn further, thinking of a "burst-shadowpool": small pool of GPU nodes marked pool=burst-shadow, used only for preemptible/fractional jobs during egress pressure. autoscaler spins them up when cluster-wide rack_egress_high > X. They can be cheaper SKUs.

nina: burst-shadowpool is nice. Operational concerns: ensure model-training heavy egress isn't routed through the same ToR if possible; otherwise pool just shifts the problem. Also need a TTL cap and eviction SLA for pods on that pool.

haresh: telemetry we need right away: histogram node.egress_5m, gauge rack.egress_percent, metric fractional_pack_coalescence (contiguous gpu-slices per node), eviction_churn_rate by node_label. Without these we can't prove improvement.

omar: initial canary plan: implement scoring plugin in staging, emit metrics, then canary RBAC + controller to escalate taint on 2 scheduler replicas in prod for a single AZ. Abort if eviction_churn_rate increases > 5% or fractional_pack_coalescence decreases.

sylvie: ops runbook actions:
- add egress_util_penalty plugin prototype (omar, 2d)
- implement soft-label-and-escalate controller (haresh, 1d)
- create burst-shadowpool autoscaler config + cost projection (nina, 1d)
- add dashboards/alerts (sylvie, 1d)

kube-bot: Taint controller deployed to staging cluster, watching node.egress_5m > 1200000000 for 2 windows.

haresh: cost note: baseline estimate shows a 0.8% steady-state increase if autoscaler keeps burst pool at low usage, worst-case 5% if we run 24/7. autoscaler TTL and scale-down aggressiveness keep it near 0.x% normally.

omar: quick staging experiment: switched scheduler candidates to sort by (gpu_contiguous - egress_penalty). contiguous slices went from 3.1 -> 3.6 avg for fractional pods, and preemptions fell ~15% in the test window. will attach logs.

nina: once plugin lands, let's gate rollout by rack-level telemetry, not global. only enable penalties for racks with > 70% egress utilization to avoid global oscillation.

sylvie: agreed. i'll file an RFC after staging results. thanks all. :thumbsup:
